title: Vigil honours man shot, killed by Timmins police
article: Close to a hundred friends and family members withstood freezing temperatures Tuesday afternoon to take part in a vigil acknowledging the death of Joey Knapaysweet, 21, who died Saturday after a shooting incident involving Timmins Police Service.
Standing in the snow at the edge of frozen Gillies Lake, several women in the group spoke about Knapaysweet as the person many remembered when he was growing up in Fort Albany.
One woman said it was important to remember the man and offer prayers to help him "on his journey to the other side".
Several in the group were openly weeping. They hugged and comforted each other, sharing their sorrow.
As the group gathered, they stood around in a circle where a bouquet of red roses was placed on the snow, beside some candles and photographs of the deceased.

Although the vigil began at 4 p.m. with a couple of dozen people, as the minutes passed more and more people began arriving on foot and in vehicles to the point where it appeared there was a crowd of about 100 who gathered quietly, shaking hands, holding hands, hugging and showing support.
